# SHAP dependence plots for the BFI-S items

This script gives the following figure: Supplementary Figure S8, SHAP Dependence Plots for the BFI-S Items in the Neural Network, including its continued page. It reads the SHAP values and the hold-out predictor values with standardised item scores saved by the neural network script.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(shapviz)
library(patchwork)

# The saved SHAP values and the hold-out predictor values with standardised item scores are loaded.
nnet_item_shap_values <- readRDS("nnet_item_shap_values.rds")
nnet_item_shap_data_standardised <- readRDS("nnet_item_shap_data_standardised.rds")
```

## Panels and sizes

```{r}
# This table gives the code, the wording, and the trait of each item. Its order sets the order of the panels.
items <- tibble::tribble(
  ~code, ~wording, ~trait,
  "BFF_15_1", "Worries a lot", "Neuroticism",
  "BFF_15_2", "Gets nervous easily", "Neuroticism",
  "BFF_15_3", "Remains calm in tense situations (reversed)", "Neuroticism",
  "BFF_15_4", "Is talkative", "Extraversion",
  "BFF_15_5", "Is outgoing, sociable", "Extraversion",
  "BFF_15_6", "Is reserved (reversed)", "Extraversion",
  "BFF_15_7", "Is original, comes up with new ideas", "Openness",
  "BFF_15_8", "Values artistic, aesthetic experiences", "Openness",
  "BFF_15_9", "Has an active imagination", "Openness",
  "BFF_15_10", "Is sometimes rude to others (reversed)", "Agreeableness",
  "BFF_15_11", "Has a forgiving nature", "Agreeableness",
  "BFF_15_12", "Is considerate and kind to almost everyone", "Agreeableness",
  "BFF_15_13", "Does a thorough job", "Conscientiousness",
  "BFF_15_14", "Tends to be lazy (reversed)", "Conscientiousness",
  "BFF_15_15", "Does things efficiently", "Conscientiousness"
)

# This factor scales the size of all points and the thickness of all lines in the panels.
nnet_item_mark <- 7.5 / 12
```

## Drawing the original dependence plot

```{r}
# shapviz draws the original dependence plot: one panel for each item, in the order of the item table.
# Each grey, semi-transparent point is one hold-out participant, with its SHAP value on the y-axis.
# The x-axis uses the standardised item scores. The points are not coloured by another predictor.
panels <- sv_dependence(
  shapviz(nnet_item_shap_values, X = nnet_item_shap_data_standardised),
  v = items$code,
  color_var = NULL,
  color = "grey70",
  share_y = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.45,
  size = 0.6 * nnet_item_mark
)
```

## Adjusting the plot

```{r}
# The original plot is then adjusted.
panels <- panels &
  # A black horizontal line is drawn at a SHAP value of zero.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6 * nnet_item_mark) &
  # The x-axis is divided into ten intervals. In each interval, a vertical bar spans the mean SHAP value plus and minus one standard deviation.
  stat_summary_bin(
    fun = mean,
    fun.min = function(y) mean(y) - sd(y),
    fun.max = function(y) mean(y) + sd(y),
    geom = "errorbar",
    bins = 10,
    width = 0.25,
    linewidth = 0.5 * nnet_item_mark
  ) &
  # A black line connects the mean SHAP values of the ten intervals.
  stat_summary_bin(aes(group = 1), fun = mean, geom = "line", bins = 10, linewidth = 0.5 * nnet_item_mark) &
  # A black point marks the mean SHAP value of each interval.
  stat_summary_bin(fun = mean, geom = "point", bins = 10, size = 1.5 * nnet_item_mark) &
  # All panels use the same axes: standardised items from -4.45 to 4.45 on the x-axis and SHAP values from -0.6 to 0.6 on the y-axis.
  # The axis titles are removed from the panels, because they are placed beside each page.
  # The panels have a white background, dashed horizontal grid lines, and black axis text.
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-4, 4, by = 2), expand = expansion(add = 0)) &
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.5, 0.5, by = 0.25), limits = c(-0.6, 0.6)) &
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-4.45, 4.45)) &
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) &
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Arial") &
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey80", linetype = "dashed"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "black"),
    plot.margin = margin(0, 7, 0, 7)
  )

# This function wraps an item wording onto two lines of at most 28 characters.
# A short wording receives a blank second line, so every subtitle has the same height.
# The script stops if a wording needs more than two lines.
two_lines <- function(text, width = 28) {
  lines <- strwrap(text, width = width)
  stopifnot(length(lines) <= 2)
  if (length(lines) == 1) lines <- c(lines, " ")
  paste(lines, collapse = "\n")
}

# These are the panel numbers of the left column (the first item of each trait)
# and of the bottom row of each page (the openness items and the conscientiousness items).
left_column <- seq(1, 15, by = 3)
bottom_row <- c(7:9, 13:15)

for (i in seq_along(panels)) {
  # Each panel receives its item code as the title and its wording as a smaller subtitle, both centred.
  panels[[i]] <- panels[[i]] +
    labs(title = items$code[[i]], subtitle = two_lines(items$wording[[i]])) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 6.5, hjust = 0.5, lineheight = 0.85, margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))
    )

  # The y-axis numbers and ticks are removed from every panel outside the left column.
  if (!(i %in% left_column)) {
    panels[[i]] <- panels[[i]] + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank())
  }
  # The x-axis numbers and ticks are removed from every panel outside the bottom row of each page.
  if (!(i %in% bottom_row)) {
    panels[[i]] <- panels[[i]] + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())
  }
}

# The original plot is one combined figure. It is separated into a list of panels, so each page can select the panels of its traits.
panels <- as.list(panels)
```

## Arranging the panels on the pages

```{r}
# This function turns a text into a figure element, optionally rotated. It is used for the axis titles and the trait labels.
figure_label <- function(text, rotation = 0) {
  wrap_elements(
    full = grid::textGrob(
      text,
      rot = rotation,
      gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 8, fontfamily = "Arial", col = "black")
    )
  )
}

# This function builds one page from a shared y-axis title, one row of three panels per trait, and a shared x-axis title.
# In the page design, each letter is one part: A is the y-axis title, each following group is a trait label and its three panels,
# and the last letter is the x-axis title. # is an empty cell.
one_page <- function(traits, layout, heights) {
  page_parts <- list(figure_label("SHAP value", rotation = 90))
  for (trait in traits) {
    page_parts <- c(
      page_parts,
      list(figure_label(trait, rotation = 90)),
      panels[items$trait == trait]
    )
  }
  page_parts <- c(page_parts, list(figure_label("Standardised BFI-S item")))
  # The first two columns hold the labels, and the last three hold the item panels.
  wrap_plots(
    page_parts,
    design = layout,
    widths = c(0.1, 0.1, 1, 1, 1),
    heights = heights
  )
}

# The first page contains neuroticism, extraversion, and openness.
# The continued page contains agreeableness and conscientiousness.
pages <- list(
  one_page(
    c("Neuroticism", "Extraversion", "Openness"),
    layout = "ABCDE\nAFGHI\nAJKLM\n##NNN",
    heights = c(1, 1, 1, 0.045)
  ),
  one_page(
    c("Agreeableness", "Conscientiousness"),
    layout = "ABCDE\nAFGHI\n##JJJ",
    heights = c(1, 1, 0.07)
  )
)

# The page heights are calculated. The first page has three trait rows and the continued page has two.
# A fixed part of the height is set aside on both pages, and the remaining height is divided across the trait rows,
# so each trait row has the same height on both pages.
first_page_height <- 19.94
fixed_height <- 0.86
page_heights <- c(
  first_page_height,
  2 * (first_page_height - fixed_height) / 3 + fixed_height
)
```

## Saving the figure

```{r}
# The first page is saved as the first PDF of Supplementary Figure S8, and the second page as its continued page.
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)
page_files <- c(
  "figures/figure_shap_item_dependence_nn_1.pdf",
  "figures/figure_shap_item_dependence_nn_2.pdf"
)
for (page_number in seq_along(pages)) {
  ggsave(
    page_files[[page_number]],
    plot = pages[[page_number]],
    width = 19.05,
    height = page_heights[[page_number]],
    units = "cm",
    device = cairo_pdf
  )
}
```
